div.p: ACCEPTABLE CHANGES TO PRESENT U.S.-JAPAN SECURITY TREATY

list.item: Revision of the preamble to imply greater mutuality and equality.

Revision of Article II to eliminate the requirement for U.S. consent before making certain agreements with third nations and to substitute prior consultation with the United States in such cases. An alternate acceptable revision to this article would be an undertaking on Japan’s part not to contract agreements with third nations which are in conflict with the treaty. This determination would itself require agreement of the parties to the treaty.
Provisions for a treaty expiration date at the end of a specified number of years, and then only if one of the parties submits notice of intent to terminate a stated time in advance.

Recognition that the treaty is consistent with principles of the U.N. Charter,On file in Joint Secretariat. [Footnote in the source text.] provided that the form of this recognition is consistent with the exchange of notes on this subject, dated 14 September 1957.
Guarantee of Japanese-U.S. consultation in the event of any threat to peace in the Northeast Asia area.

Guarantee that the United States and Japan recognize that an armed attack directed against the territories or areas under the administrative control of the other party would be dangerous to its own peace and safety and that both parties would act to meet the common danger in accordance with its constitutional processes.
Elimination of the current provision for the possible use of U.S. forces to quell internal disorder.

note.p: On file in Joint Secretariat. [Footnote in the source text.]

Interpretation of the Security Treaty and the Administrative Agreement as They Relate to the United Nations Charter, an Understanding effected by an exchange of notes, signed at Tokyo September 14, 1957, and entered into force the same day. For text, see 8 UST (pt. 2) 1571.
